title: CuTe DSL for GPU Kernel Development
critical_patterns: Use of tiling to optimize memory access patterns
Leveraging shared memory for data reuse
code_snippets: kernel void exampleKernel(float* data) { __shared__ float tile[BLOCK_SIZE]; ... }
for (int i = 0; i < N; i += TILE_SIZE) { ... }
constraints: Kernel functions must be defined with __global__
Maximum number of threads per block is 1024
Shared memory is limited to 48KB per block
Avoiding warp divergence is crucial for performance
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL is a specialized language designed to simplify the development of GPU kernels by providing high-level abstractions and optimizations. It focuses on optimizing memory access patterns and parallel execution to achieve high performance. Key concepts include the use of tiling to manage memory efficiently, leveraging shared memory to reduce global memory accesses, and employing thread coarsening and loop unrolling to minimize execution overhead. Critical patterns involve structuring code to maximize data reuse and minimize latency, such as by using shared memory for frequently accessed data and organizing threads to avoid divergence. Constraints include adhering to the limits of the GPU architecture, such as the maximum number of threads per block and shared memory size. Developers must also be mindful of warp divergence, which can significantly impact performance. The DSL provides constructs to express these patterns succinctly, allowing for more readable and maintainable code. By using CuTe, developers can focus on algorithmic improvements while the DSL handles low-level optimizations.
